To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Eps1 is the first membrane‐bound PDI family member that functions as a chaperone in the quality control of proteins in the endoplamic reticulum (see also Figure 6).
Eps1 is involved in ER quality‐control mechanisms that are important for proper ER export of proteins.
Eps1, a new PDI‐related ER protein, is involved in the quality control of membrane proteins in yeast.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of protein folding, quality control and degradation in the ER.
the molecular mechanism of protein quality control in the ER.
the mechanism of protein quality control in the endoplamic reticulum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Eps1 protein acts as a chaperone in the endoplamic reticulum (Eps1 is an ER chaperone).
Eps1 is an essential PDI family member involved in ER quality assurance.
the Eps1 protein is a novel membrane‐associated PDI‐related chaperone that functions in ER quality control to ensure that only properly folded proteins are allowed to exit the ER.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ER quality control system in yeast consists of two major components: Eps1 and Hrd1.
Eps1 is the first PDI‐related chaperone involved in the ER quality control system.
Eps1 is an essential ER chaperone that is required for ER retention and degradation of misfolded proteins, and is also involved in ER export of some proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Eps1 acts like a chaperone to help the misfolded protein Pma1‐378N fold correctly.
Eps1 acts to retain misfolded membrane proteins in the ER, and this function can be separated from its ability to catalyze disulfide bond formation.
Eps1 is the first membrane‐bound chapperone identified in the yeast ER, and it functions in the ER quality control process.
